reason: The text presents Yahweh as disciplinary but ultimately protective and redemptive toward the Hebrew people. While God does deliver Israel to Philistine oppression for forty years as punishment for their evil (וַיִּתְּנֵ֧ם יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד־ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים אַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה), this is presented as a consequence of their own wrongdoing, not as antagonism. Immediately following this punishment, Yahweh provides deliverance through Samson, whom He empowers repeatedly (וַתִּצְלַ֨ח עָלָ֜יו ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֗ה). The narrative demonstrates Yahweh listening to prayers, providing strength and sustenance, and ultimately enabling Israel's salvation from oppression—all indicators of divine concern rather than antagonism.
